title: TEDxEast - Nancy Duarte uncovers common structure of greatest communicators 11/11/2010
author: TEDx Talks
description:
TEDxEast INTERCONNECTIVITY - 11.11.10: -Nancy Duarte- That Resonates with Me!

Why are some presentations spellbinding and some not? Well, this is the question Nancy Duarte takes on as she shares with the audience the secret of an excellent presentation.  In this fascinating talk Nancy Duarte explains the model that she developed for designing transformative presentations.  She explains the essential qualities of an excellent presentation by analyzing the speeches of Martin Luther King and Steve Jobs.   She reminds us that the only way to spread important ideas is to make sure that one is communicating his or her ideas effectively using strong presentation skills.  

About TEDx, x=independently organized event
In the spirit of ideas worth spreading, TEDx is a program of local, self- organized events that bring people together to share a TED-like experience. At a TEDx event, TEDTalks video and live speakers combine to spark deep discussion and connection in a small group. These local, self-organized events are branded TEDx, where x=independently organized TED event. The TED Conference provides general guidance for the TEDx program, but individual TEDx events are self-organized.*

title: Sell What's on the Truck: The Importance of Present Value in Positioning
author: aprildunford
description:
In positioning, we have to stay focused on the value of what we sell today and not lean too much on what's coming down the pipe. 

It's tempting to try to sell customers the entire grand vision of what we expect our product to be in the future. The vision generally sounds really cool! It's extra confusing for founders who have raised money on a big ambitious vision - hey, the VCs loved this story, why wouldn't it work for customers?

The problem is that most companies (unlike investors) aren't going to trade today's dollars for tomorrow's promises. In this economy, in particular, buyers want to know what you can do for them right now in exchange for the dollars they will give you right now. If we lean too much into our vision, we give those customers a good reason to delay a purchase. Why not wait it out and see if the future unfolds as you are predicting? 

Your positioning is going to shift over time. The critical thing to remember is that at each step, you have to focus on the value you can deliver right now.  As my old boss used to say - we can only sell what's on the truck.

title: The Anatomy of a Great Cold Sales Pitch
author: weskao
description:
This is the best cold sales pitch I've ever gotten. The salesperson barely mentions their company, and when they do, it’s through the lens of how their recipient benefits.

This note was from 3-4 years ago, and it was pretty groundbreaking at the time. I annotated the note to train my team at Maven about what an excellent sales pitch looks like.

Nowadays, there are a lot of cold DMs that start with a fake compliment from a tech bro, then go straight into facetiously offering value: “I’ll cut to the chase. Wanna see how we can 5x your growth in ten days? Hit me back and I’ll send what I created for you.”

This note was not that. It felt sincere and personal. And the impact of great messaging is tangible:

Not only did I join their platform and become a power user, I even became friends with the salesperson after they joined another company!

The brilliant thing is this note only has three customized sentences and they’re all in the first paragraph—the rest is boilerplate. The boilerplate was laser focused on the customer's needs, so the overall effect is the note feels personal AND it's scalable too.

Takeaway: When you frame 90% around how your recipient benefits, they are much more likely to take action.

___

It's Wednesday morning, which means my newsletter this week is now live. I wrote about why your requests should be framed 90% around your recipient.
